title: Source-traced active joint price/news numerical feature dictionary
scope: Additive documentation of the registered scheduler-v2 joint model source bytes. Source/configuration inspection only: no runtime module import, model execution, DB read, network access, live state verification, performance inference or order authority.

naming_and_order.feature_id_policy: Stable documentation IDs. The eight news IDs exactly equal NEWS_FEATURES. The 24 price and two interaction IDs are documentation-assigned names for unnamed positional entries, not claimed existing code symbols.
naming_and_order.exact_source_order: For windows 1,5,15,30,60 minutes, append (rate,span/minutes,1-density,float(not available)); then append RMS elapsed change, max gap, len(current)/61, session age; then NEWS_FEATURES tuple; then technical[0]*news[0], technical[0]*news[4].
naming_and_order.static_reconstruction_method: Read PARAMETERS['feature_windows_minutes'], the _features loop/extend calls, NEWS_FEATURES and _joint_features. This dictionary does not import or execute them. Their sequence is the expected ordering for independent AST-only validation.

shared_definitions.price: P(u) is the positive finite close field from the selected instrument's captured M1 CSV. The parser verifies instrument/granularity/complete flags if those columns exist, monotonically increasing exact minute starts, captured-byte hashes and u+60<=actual observation. It does not establish whether close is bid, ask or midpoint; that meaning is an upstream data contract, not inferred here.
shared_definitions.time: t is a UTC M1 start epoch. S(t) is the first retained row in the current session, reset only when an adjacent observed gap is greater than 1800 seconds. W(t) contains actual epochs from max(S(t),t-3600) through t inclusive. T_w is the suffix of W(t) with epochs >=t-60w. No prior-left-edge interpolation is used.
shared_definitions.pip: pip is the registered pair pip size, validated as one of 0.0001, 0.001 or 0.01 by the numeric source. Returns in pips divide price-unit differences by pip; positive means the base/quote rate rose.
shared_definitions.window_notation: n_w=|T_w|, d_w=(last(T_w)-first(T_w))/60, available=(n_w>=2), density=(n_w-1)/w. The anchor always exists, so T_w is nonempty. A complete w-minute window has w+1 closes and w intervals.
shared_definitions.news: e is the news frame evaluation epoch. C is the selected pair's context member list, V its vetted guarded-claim list. A member/group is pair-relevant if either currency key exists in its score map. An absent base or quote key is treated as score 0 only after pair relevance is established.
shared_definitions.zero_not_absence: No single numerical zero establishes that news or price data is absent. A price rate can be truly flat or unavailable; a news score can cancel; a news count of zero is conditional on the narrow scored-member projection. Empty context is encoded (0,0,0,1) and empty vetted evidence as (0,0,0,0). Invalid/stale/unverifiable snapshots are rejected, not silently converted to neutral.

causal_clocks.price: The CSV key is the UTC M1 start. P(t) is complete no earlier than t+60; stable-read consumer observation is retained separately and may be later. Current capture and computation require the latest close to be between 0 and 900 seconds old. Training uses actual past closes captured now and is explicitly retrospective, not proof that price files or forecasts were available then.
causal_clocks.news: Original member knowledge known_m=max(published_utc,first_seen_utc,causal_known_utc,detail_available_utc,numeric_causal_known_utc,publication_clock_known_utc) over present fields. It excludes later mapping/consumption when computing age and original expiry. Frame admission also requires a separate availability<=e.
causal_clocks.historical_news: Retained original classified members come from source_events joined to committed fast-lane mappings and independently read visibility records. Their payload/hash, visibility contract, trusted observation flag and supported original classifier version (v164 or v165) are checked. Availability=max(mapping_visible_epoch,member.observed_available_utc); the latter is at least mapping visibility. Historical frames use e=t+60, mapping<=e and known_m in [e-3600,e]. They do not reclassify mutable article tables into earlier history.
causal_clocks.current_news: Producer writes guarded joint_news_current_v1.json with as_of_utc evidence time, generated_utc after computation and source hashes. Consumer rereads/verifies it and stores a later first_observed_epoch=news_available_epoch; member observed_available_utc is raised to at least that observation. Evidence<=generated<=observation; evidence age must remain <=300 seconds. Current frame e is this actual consumer observation, not the price bar start.
causal_clocks.original_expiry: The guard sets each admitted member expiry to known_m + estimated_reaction_horizon_minutes*60. Availability includes observed_available_utc, but that later clock never moves original expiry. Within a claim expiry is the earliest representative expiry; across pair-relevant vetted groups the feature uses the earliest again. Capture expiry is min(news_evidence_epoch+300, earliest vetted pair expiry), or evidence+300 with no vetted group.
causal_clocks.price_and_news: Current price and news have distinct clocks: price can be as old as 900 seconds, news evidence at most 300 seconds, with earlier original veto expiry retained. Their interaction is a same-decision joint feature, not a claim of simultaneous arrival.
causal_clocks.fit_and_target: For training anchor t, exact P(t+3600) must exist, t+3600<=price cutoff and both endpoints must share a session. Its close matures at t+3660; news frame matures at t+60. Anchors are UTC epoch multiples of 900 seconds. Historical label y=(P(t+3600)-P(t))/pip is a training target, not one of the 34 inputs.

model_transform.training_standardization: Construct every raw feature, including both products, before normalization. For each training column j, mean_j=mean_i(x_ij), scale_j=population std_i(x_ij). Set scale_j=1 if scale_j<1e-9. Fit on z_ij=(x_ij-mean_j)/scale_j and transform the current query with those same training-only values. No query value enters the fitted mean or scale. Thus the model consumes standardized dimensionless numbers even when raw features have pips/minute or hours units.
model_transform.intercept_and_ridge: Prepend an intercept of 1 (35 design columns, not a 35th feature). beta solves (D^T D+diag(0,50,...,50)) beta=D^T y. The intercept is unpenalized. Coefficients are fitted jointly, not preset price/news conversion multipliers.
model_transform.training_readiness: Current W(t) must have >=8 actual returns and >=900 seconds span. Training requires >=48 mature exact-H1 anchors, >=12 context-nonempty rows and >=8 distinct four-field context patterns. If a vetted training dimension has std<1e-9 and its current value differs from the historical constant by >1e-9, fitting is blocked as unseen vetted input.
model_transform.training_bounds: Price capture reads a stable local CSV tail bounded to 4 MiB and 4096 rows. News reconstruction has a 48-hour committed-visibility range, 5000-row limit and explicit byte limits; violations fail closed. Model accepts at most 256 news anchor frames. Retained rows and correlated/overlapping labels are not independent sample counts.
model_transform.return_shrinkage: For N training rows, effective=N/4 is an overlap-adjusted count heuristic, shrink=effective/(effective+20). sigma=max(0.1,residual_population_std,std(y))*sqrt(1+query_leverage+1/max(effective,1)). Final expected pips=clip(raw_query_prediction*shrink,-2*sigma,2*sigma). Neither this heuristic nor numerical readiness demonstrates calibrated prediction.
model_transform.neutral_news_ablation: Use the same fitted joint coefficients, means, scales, shrinkage and joint sigma, unchanged current price features, and raw news=(0,0,0,1,0,0,0,0). Recompute products (both zero), then normalize. Joint expected minus this neutral-news expected is a model sensitivity/ablation difference, not causal news impact.
model_transform.matched_price_only: Fit a separate 24-feature Ridge model on exactly the same training anchors/targets as the joint fit. This is a comparator, not a component to add to the joint news-ablation difference.
model_transform.not_inputs: Target pips, probabilities, fitted coefficients, expected returns, spread/costs, quote-entry outcomes, source health, model scores and dashboard pair labels are not additional columns in this 34-input vector. All order/promotion/proof flags remain false.

upstream_news_mapping.producer: classify_article produces original member currency_scores. The producer later publishes guarded current topic evidence through build_current_news_snapshot(published_relevant, as_of=completed), attaches three producer source hashes and a generated clock, then writes joint_news_current_v1.json. The joint adapter independently validates/replays this artifact rather than reading the dashboard's pair_sentiment_latest.json.
upstream_news_mapping.classifier_boundary: Source title/allowed summary, extracted/issuer-bound currencies, structured release metadata, policy/risk/commodity/intervention/reported-move rules and guards determine currency_scores. These are bounded rule-generated currency hypotheses, not pips. The inspected score assembly adds monetary impulse to subject currencies, 0.65*activity direction, haven/risk-currency risk adjustments, oil-exporter/JPY oil adjustments and intervention scores; then guards can remove or zero directions. This is a traced boundary, not a complete taxonomy of every upstream parsing branch.
upstream_news_mapping.classifier_score_rules: The inspected core score finalization retains abs(score)>=0.05 and rounds clamped [-1,1] scores to six decimals. Subsequent guards include absence of causal pre-release consensus for structured numeric releases, narrative/non-catalyst/expectations context, issuer/subject currency restriction and conflicting semantic directions. The returned currency_scores is the value actually consumed; standalone research_currency_scores is not substituted.
upstream_news_mapping.context: The joint frame selects members with nonempty valid currency_scores, known_m<=e, known_m>=e-3600 and availability<=e. It deduplicates by normalized headline before selecting the pair. C contains selected members with either pair currency key. It does NOT require each context member to pass directional timeliness, corroboration or other directional guard checks. No source-quality weighting or time decay is applied in the four context aggregates. This is scored-member context, not all news text.
upstream_news_mapping.vetted: The same selected members are greedily grouped when each new member satisfies same_claim with every existing member. guard_topic evaluates each group at e. Every representative must have its own current clocks, forward_signal_timely true, publication-arrival lag within its 0..30-minute limit, unexpired original 1..1440-minute horizon, valid nonzero score map and valid quality/confidence. Context/prior-move/bootstrap/research-only and related flags exclude directional admission. Duplicate IDs invalidate support; repeated publishers or exact syndicated headlines collapse. Coherence and either >=1 source_verified member or >=2 independent representatives are required.
upstream_news_mapping.within_claim_scores: For each currency c, use w_i=max(0.1,source_quality_i) only among representatives containing c, then v_j[c]=round(sum_i(w_i*c_i[c])/sum_i(w_i),6). Every claim is equally weighted in the later pair-level average regardless of its publisher count. Claim direction is discarded if all its currency scores cancel to zero. A claim with nonzero currency scores can still have zero pair difference when its two legs are equal.
upstream_news_mapping.same_claim: Exact normalized headlines match but cannot independently corroborate. Otherwise negation sets and numeric token sets must agree; nonempty semantic-claim lists must share a canonical claim, or the fallback requires >=5 non-stopwords per headline and Jaccard word overlap >=0.8. This is a conservative implemented matching rule, not semantic truth verification.
upstream_news_mapping.not_consumed: The 34-vector does not directly consume headline text/tokens/embeddings, generic_sentiment_score, risk_off_score/risk_on_score, monetary_impulse, research_currency_scores, category one-hots, source_quality/confidence as extra scalar columns, all raw releases, dashboard directional labels, price reaction outcomes or peer-pair features. Some affect the original currency_scores or guarded eligibility upstream; many remain outside this projection.
upstream_news_mapping.limitations: Original v164/v165 classifications can differ in the historical archive; historical snapshots preserve their original classifications. Context headline deduplication is global to the frame and not a count of independent publishers. Existing source/classifier availability does not prove predictive usefulness, source completeness, or semantic correctness.

intended_inputs: P(u): selected pair's captured CSV close at actual UTC M1 start u
t: anchor UTC M1 start
pip: registered pair pip size
S(t): session start after a gap greater than 1800 seconds
features.intended_lookback: Observed closes with start u in [max(S(t), t-3600, t-1*60), t]; no earlier-neighbor interpolation at the left edge.
features.causal_warning: Price timestamp t is the UTC M1 start; its close is not available before t+60. Windows use only observed closes from the same >30-minute-gap session, preserve elapsed time and gaps, and are retrospective training inputs rather than prior prospective evidence.
gaps: Price feature names are documentation-assigned; source constructs an ordered anonymous numerical vector.
Absence of an observed minute is not diagnosed as market closure versus transport/data missingness.
features.name: Observed 1-minute window price rate
features.plain_language: Rate of observed price movement within the nominal 1-minute window, expressed in pips per elapsed minute. It is not a 1-minute forecast.
features.role: Momentum: signed observed endpoint change divided by actual elapsed minutes.
features.computation: Let T_w be the retained times in this window, n_w=|T_w|, d_w=(last(T_w)-first(T_w))/60. If n_w>=2, (P(last(T_w))-P(first(T_w)))/(pip*d_w); otherwise 0.
features.missingness: 0 is either a true zero endpoint change or a sentinel when n_w<2; span_fraction, missing_fraction and unavailable_flag accompany it.

features.name: One-hour elapsed-time RMS price change
features.plain_language: Root mean of squared adjacent observed pip changes divided by each interval's elapsed minutes.
features.role: Recent movement scale; not a demeaned volatility estimate.
intended_inputs: P(u): selected pair's captured CSV close
Actual UTC minute-start epochs u
Anchor t, session start S(t), registered pip size
features.intended_lookback: W(t): actual observations in [max(S(t),t-3600),t].
features.computation: For adjacent u_(i-1),u_i in W(t), delta_i=(P(u_i)-P(u_(i-1)))/pip and dt_i=(u_i-u_(i-1))/60. sqrt(mean_i(delta_i^2/dt_i)). The mean is over observed intervals, not elapsed-time weighted; drift is not subtracted.
features.missingness: No local zero imputation: readiness requires at least 8 actual returns and at least 15 elapsed minutes. A true flat observed window gives 0.
features.causal_warning: Price timestamp t is the UTC M1 start; its close is not available before t+60. Windows use only observed closes from the same >30-minute-gap session, preserve elapsed time and gaps, and are retrospective training inputs rather than prior prospective evidence.
gaps: Do not label this as standard deviation or assume it is an unbiased volatility estimator.
Documentation-assigned name; source vector is positional.
